```sh
kafka topic add-partitions <topics...>
```

Raise a topic to a new total partition count

## Arguments

| Argument    | Description                                |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `topics...` | topic names to raise to --count partitions |

Shared options and defaults: [connection profiles, JSON output, logging and help](../../../global-options/).

## Defaults

The requested count is the new total, not the number to add. --dry-run validates without changing the topic.

## Before you run

Increases the partition count permanently; Kafka does not support shrinking it. Key-to-partition mapping can change. Review ordering assumptions before execution.

## Flags

| Flag                 | Description                                      |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `--brokers <string>` | comma-separated broker list, e.g. localhost:9092 |
| `--count <number>`   | the new total number of partitions (not a delta) |
| `--dry-run`          | validate without changing anything               |

## Examples

```sh
kafka topic add-partitions orders --count 6 --brokers localhost:9092
kafka topic add-partitions orders payments --count 6 --dry-run
```

## Output

Illustrative, abbreviated output. Empty arrays show the result envelope; actual entries, identifiers, optional fields and broker errors depend on the request and cluster.

With `--json`:

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "topic": "events",
      "ok": true
    }
  ]
}
```

Declared exit codes: `0`, `1`, `2`, `4`. See the exit-code reference for meanings.
